info.title: Bonsai API
info.description:
The Bonsai API lets you read and write the records behind your business:
clients and contacts, deals, projects, tasks, time entries and invoices.
It is organized around REST, takes and returns JSON, and uses standard HTTP
verbs, status codes and authentication.

## Authentication

Every request is authenticated with a bearer token, sent in the
`Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer bonsai_at_...
```

There are two ways to get one, and they grant exactly the same access:

- **API key** — create one in your Bonsai settings and use it directly. Best
  for scripts and back-office integrations acting on your own account.
- **OAuth 2.1** — run the authorization code flow with PKCE to act on another
  Bonsai user's behalf. Best for applications you distribute.

A token is scoped to one Bonsai account, and it can only ever do what the
member behind it can do in the Bonsai app. A member who cannot see a project
in the app cannot see it through the API either, so plan for `403` and `404`
responses on records outside their reach.

Tokens are secrets. Never ship one in client-side code or commit it to source
control. Requests must use HTTPS; unauthenticated calls fail with `401`.

## Requests and responses

Every successful response is an object with two top-level keys:

```json
{
  "data": { "...": "the record, or an array of records" },
  "meta": { "request_id": "b1f0d2c4-7a9e-4c3b-8d5f-1e2a3b4c5d6e" }
}
```

Write endpoints take their attributes wrapped in a key named after the
resource — `{ "task": { "title": "..." } }` — and reject a body that is
missing the wrapper with `400`. `PATCH` is a partial update: only the fields
present in the body change. Sending an explicit `null` clears some fields but
is ignored on others, so check the field you are writing — every field that
can be cleared says so.

Money is serialized as a decimal string rather than a float so no precision is
lost in transit; dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` and timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC.

## Pagination

List endpoints are paginated with `page[number]` (1-indexed) and `page[size]`
(25 by default, 100 at most; larger values are silently reduced to 100).
Each list response carries the cursor in `meta.pagination`:

```json
{ "page": 1, "page_size": 25, "has_more": true }
```

Keep requesting the next page while `has_more` is `true`. There is no total
count — counting every match is expensive on large accounts, and `has_more`
is enough to walk a collection to the end.

## Filtering

List endpoints narrow results with nested `filter` parameters, such as
`?filter[status]=active`. Filters that accept several values take either a
comma-separated string or repeated array parameters:

```
?filter[priority]=high,medium
?filter[priority][]=high&filter[priority][]=medium
```

Each endpoint documents the filters it supports. An unknown filter key is an
error rather than a no-op, so a typo surfaces as `400` instead of quietly
returning the wrong records.

## Errors

Bonsai uses conventional HTTP status codes, and every failure returns the
same envelope:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "validation_error",
    "status": 422,
    "message": "Validation failed",
    "request_id": "b1f0d2c4-7a9e-4c3b-8d5f-1e2a3b4c5d6e",
    "details": [
      {
        "source": { "pointer": "/data/attributes/title" },
        "code": "blank",
        "message": "Title can't be blank"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Branch on `type` and, for field-level problems, on each entry's `code` — both
are stable, while `message` is not. `details` lists every problem at once, so
a rejected write can be fixed in a single pass. `422` means the body was
understood but rejected; `400` means the request itself could not be read.

Every response includes a `request_id`, in the body and in the
`X-Request-Id` header. Log it: it is the fastest way for support to find a
specific call.

## Rate limits

Limits are counted per credential, not per IP, so one integration cannot
spend another's budget:

| Scope | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| All requests | 600 per minute, 10,000 per hour |
| Writes (`POST`, `PATCH`, `PUT`, `DELETE`) | 120 per minute |

Exceeding a limit returns `429` with `Retry-After` and `RateLimit-*` headers
describing when to try again. Back off for at least `Retry-After` seconds —
ideally with jitter — rather than retrying immediately.

## Versioning

This is version 1 of the API, and every path is prefixed with
`/public-api/v1`. Additive changes — a new endpoint, a new optional
parameter, a new field in a response — can ship at any time, so treat
unrecognized response fields as safe to ignore. Anything that would break an
existing integration ships as a new version instead. Fields marked deprecated
keep working until the next major version.

get.description:
Lists the stages of your deal and project boards, a page at a time.

Deals move through these stages, so this is where you turn a stage name
such as `Won` into the `board_group_id` the deal endpoints take.

You only get the boards you are allowed to list: deal stages need
permission to see deals, project stages need permission to see
projects. Without either, the list comes back empty.

## Filtering

- `filter[name]` — partial, case-insensitive match on the stage name.
- `filter[resource_type]` — `Deal` or `Project`, to return one board's
  stages only. Omit it to get both.

Lists the comments on one task, newest first.

Comments always belong to a task or a
deal, so there is no
endpoint that lists them all — you read them per record. A
task you cannot see returns `404`.

Two kinds of entry live in this thread: comments people wrote

written comments come back by default; use `filter[kind]` to get the

post.description:
Posts a comment on one task, attributed to whoever the
token belongs to. `body` is the only field, and unsafe HTML is stripped
before it is stored. A task you cannot see returns
`404`.

Posting a comment notifies the people already following that task — its assignee and anyone subscribed to it. Who gets notified
is decided entirely by the task, never by what the
comment says.

**@-mentions do not work here.** Writing `@Alex` in `body` stores those
characters and nothing more: it does not link to Alex, does not notify
Alex, and there is no parameter that would. If you need to reach a
specific person, this is not the endpoint for it.

Attachments are not supported either.

get.description:
Lists the tags your account has defined, a page at a time. Every tag
type comes back in one flat collection; filter by `tag_type` to narrow
it.

A tag belongs to exactly one type of record, so a tag you intend to put
on a task must be a `task` tag. Pass the ids you find here in `tag_ids`
when creating or updating a task.

You only get the tag types you are allowed to list the underlying
records for: `task` tags need permission to see tasks, `deal` tags need
permission to see deals, and so on. A token that cannot list any of
them gets a `403`.

## Filtering

- `filter[name]` — partial, case-insensitive match on the tag name.
- `filter[tag_type]` — return one type of tag only. Omit it to get all
  types.

Ends a recurring or subscription series in one call. No further invoices
are generated, and for a subscription your client's card is no longer
charged automatically — the same thing the Bonsai app does when you end a
billing cycle.

outstanding and still needs paying, and nothing is deleted.

recent one, and that is the invoice you get back. So the `id` in the
response is often not the `invoice_id` you sent.

again. `kind` still reads `recurring` when the series issued more than

stopping a subscription also turns off the auto-send that issued it. Both
match the app.

stopped; one that never repeated is a plain one-off afterwards, and

`content` is Markdown. Bonsai converts it to the rich text the notes
editor renders, so the constructs below all survive the conversion:

- headings, `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `~~strikethrough~~`

images and mention spans survive an update but cannot be written here,

Starts tracking a budget on a project you already have. A project has at
most one budget, so creating a second one returns `422`.

`calculation_mode` sets the unit of every number in the budget: `fee`
counts money in the project's currency, `time` counts hours. `amount` is
a plain decimal in that unit, not cents — `"5000"` on a `fee` budget is
5,000.00 and `"37.5"` on a `time` budget is 37.5 hours.

`calculation_base` has to be one the mode can count, and any other is
rejected:

| `calculation_mode` | `calculation_base` |
| --- | --- |
| `fee` | `billable_time`, `billable_time_and_expenses`, `expenses` |
| `time` | `billable_time`, `non_billable_time`, `billable_and_non_billable_time` |

Every setting you leave out is taken from the company's budget settings
in Bonsai, the ones the app pre-fills. A default `calculation_base` the
mode cannot count becomes `billable_time`.

The project needs a `start_date`, because budget cycles run from it; set
one with `PATCH /public-api/v1/projects/{id}` first. A project that
starts in the future gets its budget right away, and its first cycle
opens on the start date.

A project the token cannot see returns `404`. One it can see returns
`403` when the token may not change the project or see its budget, or
when the plan does not include budgets.

and anything you leave out keeps its current value. None of them can be
cleared, so `null` or an empty string returns `422`; to stop tracking
the budget, use `DELETE /public-api/v1/projects/{id}/budget`. Keys other
than the ones below are ignored.

counts money in the project's currency, `time` counts hours. Changing it
does not convert `amount` — `"40"` stays 40, read in the new unit — so

| `calculation_mode` | `calculation_base` |
| --- | --- |
| `fee` | `billable_time`, `billable_time_and_expenses`, `expenses` |
| `time` | `billable_time`, `non_billable_time`, `billable_and_non_billable_time` |

start date, and `current_cycle` in the response is the rebuilt one. Any

Updates a project. Every field is optional, and anything you leave out
keeps its current value.

Sending `null` clears `finish_date`, `billing_fee` and `billing_cycle`.
`title`, `start_date`, `billing_type` and `board_group_id` can be
changed but not cleared.

Whenever you touch a billing field the resulting combination is checked,
not just the values you sent — so moving a `retainer` to `time` means
clearing the fee and cycle in the same request:

| `billing_type` | `billing_fee` | `billing_cycle` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fixed_fee` | required | must be empty |
| `retainer` | required | required |
| `time` | must be empty | must be empty |
| `not_billable` | must be empty | must be empty |

billing; without it the whole request is rejected with `422`
`not_accessible` and nothing is saved. Existing time entries keep the
rate they were logged at — a billing change applies to new ones only.

`finish_date` has to be on or after `start_date`, whether you send both
or only one of them — the other is taken from the project as it stands.

`board_group_id` moves the project to another stage of the project
board it is already on — a stage belonging to a different board is
rejected. Find one with
`GET /public-api/v1/board_groups?filter[resource_type]=Project`. A
project that is on no board yet can be filed onto any of them.

The client company and the currency are both fixed once a project
exists, so `company_id` and `currency` are ignored here. Amounts already
recorded against a project are never converted, so changing its currency
would silently restate them — set it when you create the project.

not change returns `403`.

for others with `filter[scope]`.

get.description:
Lists logged time, newest first, a page at a time.

What comes back depends on the token: without permission to see the whole
team's time, you only get your own entries, and
`filter[owner_member_id]` cannot reach anyone else's.

The money fields — `rate`, `billable_amount`, `non_billable` and
`billing_status` — are left out entirely for a token that is not allowed
to see billing. Treat them as optional keys rather than assuming they
are always there. The same token cannot filter on
`filter[billing_status]` either: that would hand back the value the
field is hiding, so it returns `403` instead.

## Filtering

- `filter[date_from]` and `filter[date_to]` — a date range over the day
  the work was done. Both bounds are inclusive, and either works alone.
- `filter[owner_member_id]` — one or more team member ids, or `me` for
  whoever the token belongs to.
- `filter[project_id]` — one or more project ids.
- `filter[company_id]` — one or more client company ids, matched through
  each entry's project.
- `filter[billing_status]` — `billed`, `unbilled` or `non_billable`, or
  several at once. Needs permission to see billing.
- `filter[currency]` — one or more three-letter ISO 4217 currency codes.

post.description:
Logs time. Only `seconds` and `date` are required: the account comes from
the token, and the client is taken from the project, so neither is
something you send.

Attach the entry to work with `project_id` or `task_uuid`. Sending
`task_uuid` also settles the project — it is taken from the task, and any
`project_id` you send is ignored.

Two fields depend on permissions rather than on what you send. `rate` and
`non_billable` are only honoured for a token allowed to set billing; for
anyone else Bonsai derives them from the project or member rate and the
project's billing type. Logging time against someone else's name with
`owner_member_id` needs permission to manage the whole team's time; it
defaults to whoever the token belongs to.

patch.description:
Updates a logged time entry. Every field is optional, and anything you
leave out keeps its current value.

Move the entry between projects or tasks with `project_id` and
`task_uuid`. Sending `task_uuid` also settles the project — it is taken
from the task, and any `project_id` you send is ignored. Send either as
`null` to detach.

Moving the entry to a different project recalculates `rate` and
`non_billable` from the new project unless you set them yourself.

As on creation, `rate` and `non_billable` are only honoured for a token
allowed to set billing, and reassigning `owner_member_id` to somebody
else needs permission to manage the whole team's time.

An entry already billed on a paid or in-progress invoice is frozen:
editing it fails with `422 not_accessible`. Remove the invoice line item
first if you need to change it.

Set `billing_status` to `billed` or `unbilled` to move the entry's
billing state. It is only honoured for a token allowed to set billing,
and a token without that permission gets `422 not_accessible` rather
than a silent no-op. `non_billable` is not a writable value here — use
the `non_billable` flag instead.

Marking an entry `billed` requires it to be on a project and billable,
and fails with `422 invalid_value` otherwise. Moving a billed entry out
of `billed` indirectly — by clearing its project or task, or by moving it
to a non-billable project — needs the same billing permission and fails
with `422 not_accessible` without it. An entry attached to an
invoice cannot be moved in either direction and fails with
`422 not_accessible`. Repeating `billed` re-stamps the entry with the
current time, matching the bulk action in the app; repeating `unbilled`
on an already-unbilled entry changes nothing. A request that only sets
`billing_status` is accepted on a locked timesheet, matching the app's
mark-as-billed action.

`status` and `billing_status` answer different questions. `status`
tracks whether the entry sits on an invoice, so an entry you mark billed
by hand keeps `status: unbilled` while `billing_status` reads `billed`.

type.description:
What kind of failure this is. Branch on this rather than on `message`:

- `bad_request` (400) — a query parameter is unknown, malformed or conflicts with another.
- `authentication_error` (401) — the access token is missing, expired or invalid.
- `insufficient_permissions` (403) — the token is valid but the member behind it is not allowed to do this.
- `not_found` (404) — no such record in your account.
- `validation_error` (422) — the request body was understood but rejected. See `details`.
- `rate_limited` (429) — you have exhausted a rate limit window.
- `internal_error` (500) — something failed on our side. Safe to retry.

code.description:
Machine-readable reason this field was rejected:

- `blank` — a required value was empty or missing.
- `invalid_value` — the value was the wrong shape, or outside the allowed set.
- `not_accessible` — the value names a record that does not exist in your account, or that this token may not use.
- `parameter_missing` — a required top-level wrapper was absent from the body.
- `unknown_filter` — no such `filter[...]` key on this endpoint.
- `conflicting_filters` — two filters were supplied that cannot be combined.
- `unknown_sort_field` — no such sortable field on this endpoint.
- `internal_error` — the failure could not be attributed to the request.

- `overdue` — sent, unpaid and past `due_date`.

kind.description:
How the invoice repeats:

- `single` — a one-off invoice. Scheduling one to send later does not make it
  recurring; `status` reports that as `scheduled`.
- `recurring` — reissued on `repeat_interval` until you stop it or `repeat_finish_date` arrives.
- `subscription` — recurring, and charged automatically to the card the client has on file.
- `bundled` — one of several invoices grouped to be sent and paid together.

`bundled` is read-only: bundles are assembled in the Bonsai app from
invoices that already exist, so it cannot be passed when creating one.

repeat_interval.description: How often a `recurring` or `subscription` invoice is reissued, or `null` for a one-off. It records the cadence an invoice was issued under rather than whether its series still runs: stopping a series keeps the interval on every invoice so the series can be started again, including one stopped before it repeated, which then reads `kind` `single`. Only the last invoice a series issues on `repeat_finish_date` comes back `null`. Use `recurrence_active` to tell a running series from a stopped or finished one.

repeat_finish_date.description: Date the series stops reissuing, or `null` for a one-off or a series that runs until you stop it. Only the newest invoice of a series carries it: each repeat hands the date on to the invoice it creates, so earlier invoices read `null` even when the series has an end. When the date falls a whole number of `repeat_interval`s after the issue date, the final invoice is issued on it; otherwise the series ends with the last repeat before it. Stopping a series keeps the date so the series can be started again.

series_id.description: Id of the first invoice of the series this one belongs to, the same for every invoice in it, so you can group them. `null` for an invoice that is not part of a series.

recurrence_active.description: Whether the series this invoice belongs to still reissues. Unlike `kind` and `repeat_interval`, which describe the invoice, this describes the series, so every invoice in it reports the same answer and an already-issued one turns `false` once the series is stopped. It is `true` exactly when `DELETE /invoices/{invoice_id}/recurrence` has something to stop.

content_html.description: The note body in the HTML the Bonsai editor renders, scrubbed of script-execution vectors. This is the field to send back to `PATCH /public-api/v1/notes/{id}`: read it, change what you need and return it, and everything you left alone is preserved. `null` only when the note has no body at all. Returned on single-note responses only, never in a list.

content_plain_text.description: The same body with the markup removed, for when you only need to read what the note says. It cannot be sent back — the update endpoint takes `content_html`. `null` here means the body holds no text, not that the note is empty: a note containing only an image or a table returns `null` while `content_html` returns the body. Returned on single-note responses only, never in a list.
examples: Discussed the renewal and agreed to send a revised quote.

NoteDetailedTrait.description: The body of the note, returned when you write or retrieve a single note but never in a list.

closing_date.description: Last day the cycle counts, or `null` when the budget never resets and the project is open-ended.

consumed_amount.description: How much of the budget this cycle has used, as a decimal string, in the same unit as the budget `amount`.

consumed_percentage.description: How much of the budget this cycle has used, as a whole percentage. Exceeds 100 once the budget is over.

ProjectBudgetCycle.description: One run of a budget: the window it covers and how much of the budget it has used.

amount.description: The budget ceiling as a decimal string — an amount in the project currency when `calculation_mode` is `fee`, a number of hours when it is `time`.

over_budget_notification_threshold.description: Percentage of the budget that triggers the alert, as a decimal string.

calculation_mode.description: What the budget is measured in: `fee` for money, `time` for hours.

calculation_base.description: What counts against the budget: logged time (`billable_time`, `non_billable_time`, `billable_and_non_billable_time`), billable time plus expenses (`billable_time_and_expenses`), or expenses alone (`expenses`).

expenses_calculation_base.description: Which expenses count, when `calculation_base` includes them: `billable`, `non_billable` or `all`.

reset_frequency.description: How often the budget starts over. `never` runs one cycle for the life of the project; the rest open a fresh cycle every `weekly`, `monthly` or `quarterly` period from the project start date.

over_budget_notification.description: Whether Bonsai alerts the project team when spending passes `over_budget_notification_threshold`.

current_cycle.description: The cycle running today. A project that has not started yet reports a zeroed cycle over its first window, and one that has ended keeps reporting its last. `null` only when the project has no start date.

ProjectBudget.description: A ceiling on what a project may consume — money or hours — and how often it resets.

public_url_token.description: Token in the project's client-facing URL. The list endpoint accepts it as `filter[public_url_token]`.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code the project bills in.

start_date.description: Date work on the project starts.

finish_date.description: Date work on the project ends, or `null` when it is open-ended.

sequence.description: Counter behind `number`, incrementing per client. `null` until a number has been assigned.

number.description: Human-readable project reference. `null` until one has been assigned.

board_group_id.description: Id of the pipeline stage the project's board card sits in, or `null` when the project is not on a board. Send it to `PATCH /public-api/v1/projects/{id}` to move the project to another stage.

company_name.description: Name of the client the project is for, or `null`.

client_or_company_name.description: Deprecated — read `company_name` instead, which carries the same value. This field will be removed in a future release.

billing_type.description: How the project bills: `time` (hourly), `fixed_fee` (a single agreed fee), `retainer` (a recurring fee) or `not_billable`.

billing_cycle.description: How often a retainer bills. `null` for every other billing type.

billing_fee.description: The agreed fee as a decimal string, in `currency`. Set on `fixed_fee` and `retainer` projects, `null` otherwise.

company_id.description: Id of the client company the project is for, or `null` when the client is not a company record.

url.description: Absolute link to the project in the Bonsai app. Share it to send someone straight to the record.

budget.description: The budget tracked against this project, or `null` when it has none. Omitted entirely when your token cannot see budgets.

Project.description: An engagement you deliver for a client. Tasks, logged time and invoices all hang off a project.

uuid.description: Unique identifier for the task. This is the id every task endpoint takes in its path.

number.description: Human-readable task reference. `null` until one has been assigned.

due_date.description: Date the task is due, or `null` when it is unscheduled.

start_date.description: Date work on the task starts, or `null` when unset.

time_estimate_in_minutes.description: Estimated effort in whole minutes, or `null` when no estimate is set.

priority.description: Priority bucket, or `null` when the task has no priority.

completed_at.description: When the task was marked complete, or `null` while it is still open.

archived_at.description: When the task was archived, or `null` while it is active.

assignee_id.description: User id of the assignee, or `null` when unassigned. Read-only — the create and update endpoints take `assignee_member_id` instead.

assignee_member_id.description: Team member id of the assignee, or `null` when unassigned. This is the value the create and update endpoints accept.

creator_member_id.description: Team member id of whoever created the task.

project_id.description: Id of the project the task belongs to, or `null` for a task that stands on its own.

billable.description: Whether time logged against this task can be billed to the client. Absent unless the token is allowed to see billing.

deal_id.description: Id of the deal the task belongs to, or `null` when it is not attached to a deal. Absent unless the token is allowed to see deals.

parent_task_uuid.description: `uuid` of this task's parent when it is a subtask, `null` for a top-level task.

project_title.description: Title of the project the task belongs to, or `null`.

assignee_member_name.description: Name of the assignee, or `null` when the task is unassigned.

url.description: Absolute link to the task in the Bonsai app. Resolves to the task on its project board, or to the standalone task list when it belongs to no project.

task_status.description: The board column the task currently sits in, or `null` when it has no status.

company_tags.description: Tags applied to the task. Only `id` and `name` are returned here — list the tags endpoint for a tag's type and color.

Task.description: A unit of work, optionally inside a project and optionally nested under a parent task.

description_html.description: Task description as an HTML fragment, sanitized to a safe set of tags. Returned on single-task responses only, never in a list.

description_plain_text.description: Task description with all HTML removed. Returned on single-task responses only, never in a list.

TaskDetailedTrait.description: The description fields returned when you retrieve a single task, but never in a list.

id.description: Unique identifier for the status. Pass this value as `task_status_id` when creating or updating a task.

status.description: Status name as it appears on the board.

state.description: Whether tasks in this status count as open (`active`) or finished (`complete`).

color.description: Hex color the status is drawn in, or `null` when it has none.

position.description: Position of the status on the board, ordered left to right.

TaskStatus.description: A column of your task board. Moving a task between statuses is how you track its progress.

user_id.description: Id of the Bonsai user behind the membership, or `null` for an invitation nobody has accepted yet.

deactivated_at.description: When an administrator deactivated the member, or `null`. A member with a value here has no access, whatever `confirmed_at` says.

confirmed_at.description: When the member accepted their invitation, or `null` while it is still outstanding.

declined_at.description: When the member declined their invitation, or `null`. Never set alongside `confirmed_at`.

company_member_id.description: Unique identifier for the membership. This is the value write endpoints accept as `assignee_member_id` or `owner_member_id`.

name.description: The member's full name, or `null` before they accept their invitation.

role.description: The member's job title, for example `Software Engineer`. Free text set by your team, `null` when unset. It carries no authorization meaning — see `permission_profile` for that.

permission_profile.description: Name of the permission profile that decides what the member is allowed to do, for example `Owner` or `Collaborator`. `null` when unset.

TeamMember.description: Somebody's membership of your Bonsai account, and the ids you use to assign work to them.

name.description: The name itself. Pass it verbatim to the filter named by `kind`.

kind.description: Which filter on the template list accepts this name: `category` feeds `filter[category]`, `industry` feeds `filter[industry]`.

TemplateCategory.description: One name a template can be filed under, and the filter that accepts it.

id.description: Unique identifier for the template. Stable across requests, so you can store it and recognise the same template later.

name.description: Template name, as it appears in the gallery.

region.description: The region whose conventions the template is written for, or `null` when it applies everywhere.

updated_at.description: When the template was last changed.

source.description: Where the template comes from: `own` for one your account saved, `library` for one of Bonsai's. Prefer your own when both match.

categories.description: Category names the template is filed under, drawn from the `category` rows of `/public-api/v1/template_categories?filter[type]=Doc`. Your own templates are filed under `My Templates`.

industries.description: Industry names the template is aimed at, drawn from the `industry` rows of `/public-api/v1/template_categories?filter[type]=Doc`.

url.description: Absolute link to open the template in the Bonsai app, or `null` when your account cannot edit it. Library templates are edited by Bonsai, so theirs is `null` unless your account curates the library; your own is `null` when your role cannot edit documents.

Template.description: A template you can start new work from — one your account saved, or one from Bonsai's library.

roles.description: The parts a document made from this template expects somebody to fill.

TemplateDocTrait.description: The extra fields a document template carries on top of the fields every template has.

key.description: Unique identifier for the time entry. This is the id the update endpoint takes in its path.

seconds.description: Duration of the entry in seconds.

notes.description: What the time was spent on, or `null`.

rate.description: Hourly rate applied to the entry, as a decimal string in `currency`. `null` when no rate applies. Absent unless the token is allowed to see billing.

non_billable.description: Whether the entry is excluded from billing. Absent unless the token is allowed to see billing.

billable_amount.description: What the entry bills for, as a decimal string in `currency`. Absent unless the token is allowed to see billing.

status.description: Whether the entry has been placed on an invoice. `billing_status` is the fuller picture, and is what the list filter matches on.

project_id.description: Id of the project the time is logged against, or `null` when the entry is not attached to one.

owner_member_id.description: Team member id of whoever the time is logged for, or `null`.

billing_status.description: Effective billing state: `non_billable`, `unbilled` (billable, not on an invoice yet) or `billed` (on an invoice that has been sent, is overdue, is awaiting payment or has been paid, or marked billed by hand). Accepted by `filter[billing_status]` on the list endpoint, and writable as `billed` or `unbilled` on the update endpoint. Absent unless the token is allowed to see billing.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for `rate` and `billable_amount`.

task_uuid.description: `uuid` of the task the entry is linked to, or `null` when it is logged against a project only.

TimeEntry.description: Time logged against a project or task, and the basis for billing hourly work.

tags.name: Companies
tags.description: Client companies in your CRM. The API calls them companies; they are what deals, projects and invoices are billed to.

tags.name: Contacts
tags.description: The people you work with at your client companies. A contact can be linked to more than one company, or to none at all.

tags.name: Deals
tags.description: Opportunities moving through your sales pipeline. Each deal sits in one stage of the deal board.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: Engagements you deliver for a client, and the container tasks, time entries and invoices hang off.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description: Units of work, optionally inside a project, optionally nested under a parent task.

tags.name: Time Entries
tags.description: Time logged against a project or task, and the basis for billing hourly work.

tags.name: Invoices
tags.description: Bills you send to a client, and the line items on them.

tags.name: Comments
tags.description: Discussion threads on a task or a deal, plus the activity entries Bonsai records automatically.

tags.name: Notes
tags.description: What you write down about a client, a project or a contact. A note can be attached to several records at once, or to none.

tags.name: Board Groups
tags.description: The stages of your deal and project boards. Read these to turn a stage name into the id write endpoints expect.

tags.name: Task Statuses
tags.description: The columns of your task board. Read these to turn a status name into the id write endpoints expect.

tags.name: Company Tags
tags.description: Labels your account applies to clients, deals, projects, tasks, time entries and expenses.

tags.name: Team Members
tags.description: The people in your Bonsai account. Read these to turn a name into the id assignment fields expect.

tags.name: Templates
tags.description: The templates you can start new work from — the ones your account has saved, plus Bonsai's own library. Today that means documents.

tags.name: Documents
tags.description: Proposals, contracts and other documents your clients review and sign. Documents made through the API are drafts: you review and send them in Bonsai.
